title: Kjøp av konsulenttjenester - Produktområdeleder for produktområde landdyr
description: Formålet med anskaffelsen er å styrke Mattilsynets arbeid innen produktutvikling gjennom innleie av en erfaren konsulent som skal ivareta rollen som produktområdeleder og samtidig ha ansvar som produktleder for ett av områdets produktteam – Produktteam legemidler. Produktområde Landdyr består i dag av fire produktteam med ulike ansvarsområder. Teamene arbeider i stor grad selvstendig, men har samtidig avhengigheter og behov for samordning knyttet til retning, prioriteringer og måloppnåelse. Produktområdet er nyetablert og som produktområdeleder vil konsulentens hovedoppgave være å samarbeide med produktteamene om å finne en hensiktsmessig organisering av området fremover. Samtidig blir det viktig å utvikle og forvalte områdestrategien for Landdyr sammen med teamene, legge til rette for tydelige prioriteringer på tvers av teamene, håndtere avhengigheter og sikre god koordinering mot sponsorgruppe og øvrige interessenter. I tillegg må områdeleder følge opp at området samlet skaper ønskede resultater og effekter i tråd med Mattilsynets strategier og ambisjoner.

title: Kjøp av konsulenttjenester - Produktområdeleder for produktområde landdyr
description: Formålet med anskaffelsen er å styrke Mattilsynets arbeid innen produktutvikling gjennom bruk av erfaren konsulent som gjennom rollen som produktområdeleder skal støtte etableringen og videreutviklingen av Produktområde landdyr. Produktområde Landdyr består i dag av fire produktteam med ulike ansvarsområder hvor det er avhengigheter mellom teamene og funksjoner i øvrige deler av virksomheten. Ansvarsområdet er bredt og omfatter alt fra digitale tilsynsløsninger for landdyr, kjøttkontrollsystem på slakterier, personellgodkjenning, bruk av veterinære legemidler, samt sentrale registre. Teamene har over tid opparbeidet betydelig domenekunnskap og arbeidet selvstendig med sine oppdrag, men det er behov for å fremstå enhetlig, og sammen sikre effektene på tvers som bidrar til økt mattrygghet, dyrehelse og dyrevelferd. Konsulentens hovedoppgave vil være å koordinere og understøtte dette samarbeidet, og sammen med produktlederne bidra til å etablere tydelige rammer for organisering, styring og samhandling på produktområdet. Arbeidet skal bygge videre på teamenes eksisterende kompetanse, erfaringer og eierskap til domenet. Oppdraget innebærer å støtte utviklingen av en felles områdestrategi med tydelige mål og prioriteringer i tråd med virksomhetens strategiske ambisjoner. Konsulenten skal bidra til å etablere gode arbeidsformer for helhetlige beslutninger, håndtering av avhengigheter og oppfølging av områdets resultater og effekter i samarbeid med produktlederne, ledergruppen i Avdeling utvikling, og andre relevante interessenter. Et sentralt mål med oppdraget er å styrke produktområdets evne til å utvikle felles retning og samarbeide på tvers over tid. Konsulenten skal derfor legge vekt på involvering, kompetanseoverføring og eierskap hos eksisterende produktledere, slik at Mattilsynet selv kan videreføre produktområdeledelsen etter oppdragets avslutning.

title: Belgium – Airport equipment – Installatie, huur, onderhoud en ondersteuning van Layer-2 netwerkverbindingen tussen de skeyes datacenters te Steenokkerzeel en verschillende remote locaties van het skeyes nation-wide WAM-systeem
description: skeyes a l’intention de conclure un ou plusieurs contrats avec un ou plusieurs adjudicataires pour l’installation, la location, la maintenance et le support de connexions réseau Layer 2 entre les data centres de skeyes à Steenokkerzeel et plusieurs sites distants du système nationwide WAM de skeyes, dans une architecture en étoile (hub-spoke), afin de soutenir les phases 2A, 2B et 3 du projet WAM national (nationwide). title: Germany – Structural shell work – Neubau Marion-Dönhoff-Schule (MDS) mit Stadtteilhaus
description: Der Bauherr beabsichtigt den Neubau der Marion-Dönhoff-Schule mit Stadtteilhaus an der Möwenstraße 40 in 26388 Wilhelmshaven zu errichten. Es sind drei rechteckige Gebäude in konventioneller Betonbauweise, Stahlbetondecken (außer Sporthallendach, dort Trapezblech auf Holzbindern) und genutzten Flachdächern geplant, die mit Verbindungsgängen verbunden sind. Haus 1: Abmessung B/L ca. 31,5/ 45 m, 3-geschossig Haus 2: Abmessung B/L ca. 31,5/ 50 m, 3-geschossig Haus 3: Abmessung B/L ca. 45,5/ 69 m, 1- u. 2-geschossig Zunächst erfolgt ausschließlich die Ausführung der Rohbauarbeiten. Ca. ab Juli 2027 bis November 2028 werden Rohbau- und Ausbauarbeiten parallel durchgeführt. Das Baustellenumfeld ist durch Wohnbebauung, Bildungs- und Kinderbetreuungseinrichtungen, Sportanlagen und weitere öffentliche Nutzungen geprägt. Hieraus ergeben sich erhöhte Anforderungen an die Organisation des Baustellenverkehrs sowie an die Sicherung gegenüber unbeteiligten Dritten. title: 26-58007 Mobile Ground Control Station (MGCS) and Cargo Trailer for Drone Field Operations
description: 26-58007 Mobile Ground Control Station (MGCS) and Cargo Trailer for Drone Field Operations The National Research Council of Canada (NRC) Centre for Drone Innovation (CDI), part of the Drone and Flight Autonomy Laboratory (DFAL), requires the design, integration, and delivery of a Mobile Ground Control Station (MGCS) and complementary enclosed cargo trailer (collectively referred to as the “MGCS System”). The MGCS System will support experimental flight data acquisition and processing in remote environments, and in-situ demonstrations of novel applications of unmanned aerial systems (UAS), counter-UAS technologies, and mobile sensor networks. It will support research activities in: • Concurrent multi-UAV operations, including ground robots; • Exploration and Mapping, and Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) applications; • Electronic Warfare (EW), Security, Counter-measures deployment, and drone threat mitigation; • BVLOS experimentation; and • AI/autonomy research. Background Researchers at the NRC-CDI regularly conduct outdoor experiments and advanced technology demonstrations at remote test locations for government and industrial clients. These activities require transporting multiple drones, instrumentation, computing systems, field equipment, and crew. Current deployments require multiple transport vehicles and significant setup time. The MGCS System is intended to consolidate these capabilities with efficient reliable operations into a mobile platform. 1.0 Requirement: The MGCS System must operate as an extension of NRC’s laboratory computing, and communications infrastructure and enable rapid deployment to remote field locations, with flight testing and data collection activities commencing within approximately 30 minutes of arrival. Given the fast development pace of UAS and C-UAS technologies, the MGCS System must be modular in its design approach and implementation to support future expansion, subsystems replacements, and integration of future sensors, communications equipment, computing infrastructure upgrades, and mission systems. The requirements identified in the following subsections represent NRC's fundamental requirements for the MGCS System and are intended to describe the minimum functionality, features, and performance objectives sought under this SOR. The requirements are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all components, features, or accessories that may be required to provide a complete and operational solution. Where appropriate, Offerors may propose equivalent or alternative solutions, products, features, components, or configurations, provided that the proposed recommendation meets or exceeds the functional, operational, and performance requirements specified in this Statement of Requirement. Offerors should clearly identify any proposed substitutions and provide sufficient technical information and rationale to demonstrate equivalency. Offerors may also identify optional features, enhancements, or add-ons that are not included in the proposed compliant solution. Any such optional items must be clearly identified and priced separately in the Annex Basis of Payment and will not form part of the evaluation unless expressly stated otherwise in the solicitation. Following contract award, NRC's Technical Authority will work collaboratively with the successful Offeror during the design phase in a stage-gate review process to refine and finalize the requirements, system layouts, integration details, equipment list, and implementation plan to ensure the MGCS System is optimized for NRC's current and future evolving operational needs. Any resulting refinements must remain within the scope of the Contract and shall not reduce the minimum technical requirements specified herein. Please refer to tender documents for the Specifications.

title: Temperature Cycling Chambers
description: The National Research Council of Canada (NRC) requires the procurement of temperature cycling chambers to support the thermal evaluation of advanced energy storage technologies. As lithium-ion battery systems continue to increase in energy density and are deployed across transportation, aerospace, and stationary energy storage applications, controlled temperature testing is essential to understand how these systems perform under a range of environmental conditions. Temperature cycling chambers provide a controlled thermal environment in which battery cells, modules, and associated components can be exposed to defined temperature conditions during operation. This capability enables the evaluation of battery performance, reliability, and durability while operating across the temperature ranges encountered in real-world applications. The objective of this procurement is to provide the Automotive and Surface Transportation (AST) team with the capability to conduct controlled temperature testing of battery system and system reliability. The AST team operates a unique Canadian facility dedicated to evaluating battery cells and modules well beyond their normal operating envelopes. This procurement will enhance our laboratory infrastructure to meet the rigorous testing demands of the military, aerospace, and light-duty transportation sectors. All deliverables must be received no later than 18 weeks after contract award.

title: Mediator Consultant - Saskatchewan for the Farm Debt Mediation Service (FDMS)
description: The Programs Branch (PB) of Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada (AAFC) has requirements on an "as and when requested" basis for professional resources with expertise and skillsets for the delivery of financial counselling and mediation services. This requirement is to establish a Task Authorization Contract with a qualified Contractor's for services in Saskatchewan. It is intended to result in the award of 5 (five) contracts for 5 (five) years. The Farm Debt Mediation Service (FDMS) offers free financial counselling and mediation services to farmers who are having difficulties meeting their financial obligations. It is a voluntary, private and confidential service that brings farmers and their creditors together with a Mediator in a neutral forum to reach a mutually acceptable solution. The FDMS Administrator will assign a Financial Consultant and a Mediator to work with the farmer through the mediation process. Confidentiality is extremely important to the quality and effectiveness of the service. Information obtained from the farmer and their creditor(s) is used for the sole purpose of mediation and is shared only among the parties involved in the mediation process. The Mediator will facilitate communication between the farmer and their creditor(s), guide them through the mediation process, and remain neutral throughout. The Mediator will work collaboratively with the Financial Consultant to understand the context of the file, including the recovery plan developed by the farmer and the Financial Consultant. The Mediator will lead the mediation meeting and work with the parties toward a mutually acceptable solution. When the farmer and their creditor(s) reach an agreement, the Mediator will prepare the written arrangement and obtain the signatures of all participants

title: Montenegro – Radiotherapy devices and supplies – Supply of HDR Brachytherapy System within LIFEGATE project
description: Cardiovascular and oncological diseases remain the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in Montenegro and the wider cross-border region. According to GLOBOCAN 2020 data, Montenegro recorded 3,184 new cancer cases and 1,765 cancer-related deaths. With the expected increase in cancer incidence, an ageing population, and existing healthcare challenges, improving early detection, diagnostics, and access to specialised treatment is becoming increasingly important. The Clinical Centre of Montenegro (CCM), as the country's leading tertiary healthcare institution, plays a crucial role in providing specialised oncology services. Through this project, CCM aims to strengthen its diagnostic and treatment capacities, introduce advanced medical technologies, and improve the quality and accessibility of cancer care. A particular focus is placed on early lung cancer detection and the improvement of radiotherapy treatment, including the application of advanced techniques such as stereotactic radiotherapy and brachytherapy. These approaches are expected to contribute to more precise and effective treatment, improved patient outcomes, and better survival rates. Brachytherapy represents an important component of the planned improvements at CCM, offering opportunities to enhance treatment efficiency and quality for patients with various malignancies, particularly cervical, prostate, oesophageal, and lung cancers. The project will also support the development of innovative digital solutions, improved cancer prevention and screening programmes, and the modernisation of healthcare infrastructure through new equipment and professional training. Through cooperation with healthcare institutions in Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Clinical Centre of Montenegro will contribute to strengthening cross-border collaboration, exchanging medical expertise, and promoting common standards in cancer prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. Ultimately, the project aims to improve access to modern oncology services, enhance treatment outcomes, and strengthen the long-term capacities of the Clinical Centre of Montenegro, benefiting patients in Montenegro and the wider cross-border region.

title: Germany – Risk or hazard assessment for construction – Rahmenvertrag Kampfmittelsondierung
description: Ziel dieser Ausschreibung ist die Vergabe von Leistungen im Rahmen des Kampfmittelsondierung. Das Fernwärmenetz der Wärme Hamburg befindet sich mit seinen 900 km fast vollständig im Stadtgebiet nördlich der Elbe. Im Zuge von Neubau-, Störungs- und Umlegungsarbeiten werden geplant wie auch ungeplant Bauvorhaben abgewickelt. Sofern langfristig planbar werden Auskünfte zu Kampfmitteln eingeholt und Sondierungen vor Baubeginn durchgeführt. Häufig ist die Sondierung allerdings baubegleitend nötig. Zur Erfüllung der behördlichen Auflagen haben wir bereits seit vielen Jahren mehrere Rahmenvertragspartner unter Vertrag. Für die Abgabe eines Angebots ist die Durchführung eines Teilnahmewettbewerbs zwingend erforderlich.

title: Correct Electrical Deficiencies
description: SOW 565-22-500 Correct Electrical Deficiencies Fayetteville VAMC Intent The project consists of correcting electrical deficiencies as noted from previous VA facility assessments. Improvements include; New electrical entrance building, medium voltage loop replacement, replace electrical distribution equipment, ground conductor corrections, incidental electrical equipment cleanup throughout the Fayetteville VAMC, and minor HVAC and Plumbing improvements. Period of performance 1,174 calendar days. Medium Voltage VA owned medium voltage loop and entrance equipment will be modified or replaced with the following scope: Replace existing medium voltage entrance equipment with new at campus entrance. Provide new building: Slab on grade, brick on CMU wall, Slate roof tile (to match existing facility) Provide new VA owned medium voltage cables in concrete encased duct bank for medium voltage loop. Approximately 300 . Demo and remove old VA owned medium voltage entrance metal shack. Replace medium voltage sectionalized switch. Provide new metal-clad switchgear with draw-out vacuum circuit breakers. Replace medium voltage oil filled transformer (1) Panel Replacement and Branch Circuit Improvements Correct deficiencies to electrical panels and branch circuit wiring which are not correctly sized, protected, or are at end of useful life, as identified through various inspections over the years. o All work will be phased. All replacements to existing equipment will require the contractor to filled-out a phasing plan for VA approval. All replacements to existing equipment will require a temporary power solution to minimize electrical outage to existing areas. Such deficiencies include: Replace-in-same-room building entrance and large distribution equipment: Normal (service entrance) Switchboards: approx. 2 Generator switchboards: approx. 2 Automatic transfer switch: approx. 7 Replace-in-place distribution panels and panelboards distribution equipment Distribution Panels: approx. 5 Panelboards: approx. 68 Replace undersized feeders Redundant Gound Provide redundant equipment grounding conductor to a portion of the facility. Approx. 100,000 square feet of existing electrical branch circuit distribution in occupied space. HVAC And Plumbing Reroute (vertically & horizontally) Sewer piping and hot water piping to avoid electrical room. Provide exhaust fan to new Medium Voltage building. Incidental Electrical Equipment Cleanup Provide Identification tag to new and existing equipment throughout the facility: approx. 100 tags Clean debris from existing electrical enclosures throughout the facility: approx. 30 enclosures. Correct panel grounding, terminate cable directly to existing panel s ground bar: approx. 30 panels. ALTERNATE NO.1: BASE BID except delete Bldg 1, Floor 1 and Floor 3 of deficiency item 134 which directs the contractor to provide ground conductors in existing conduit. Which is noted on Sheet B01-E200.

title: SWL Reverse Industry Day Forum
description: Please join the Little Rock District Contracting Division for Reverse Industry Day. ALL are welcome to attend, collaborate, and share feedback, whether you are a Small or Large Business, a Prime or a Subcontractor. Details ? Date Wednesday, December 8, 2026 ? Time 9:00 AM � 12:00 PM (Central Time) Come and go as you please! ?Location University of Arkansas Division of Agriculture Cooperative Extension Service Auditorium (Not on UALR campus) 2301 South University Ave, Little Rock, AR 72204 ? Format In-Person Only (Virtual options not available for this event) ? Host Ms. Staci Allen Directions: After turning onto the campus, continue straight, toward the circular drive/large flag poles. Parking is provided in front of the building, with an overflow parking lot behind the Jack Stephens Event Center. Entrance doors are in front of the circular drive. After entering the building, entrance to the education wing (auditorium) is located to the left side of the reception desk. Parking is FREE! ? What is a Reverse Industry Day? This event is designed as a two-way dialogue. We want to hear from you! The USACE Little Rock District Team will share the latest federal contracting updates, but our primary goal is to learn how we can better support your business in our district's acquisitions. What to Expect: Open Discussion: A casual environment to ask questions, suggest acquisition improvements, and discuss federal contracting topics. Come & Go: You do not need to stay the whole time. Drop in whenever your schedule allows between 9:00 AM and 12:00 PM CST. Follow-up: The USACE Little Rock District Contracting team will share industry feedback with district leadership and post answers/findings to the Office of Small Business website. What NOT to Expect (Important Boundaries): No One-on-Ones: Private meetings or 1-on-1 capability briefings will NOT be offered. ? Focus Topics While the floor is open to your questions, the Contracting team will also share updates on the following key topics: Other Transaction Authority (OTA): Highlights from the new USACE Playbook (Dated 12 June 2026). Market Intelligence: Current and future projects procured via OTAs. REGISTRATION Please use the following link to register: https://www.cognitoforms.com/SWL3/SWLReverseIndustryDay. Each attendee requires their own individual entry. ? Looking Ahead USACE Little Rock District will also hold an Industry Day Event in Q2 of 2027. One on one capability briefs will be open to registrants who sign up. So be on the lookout for the registration notification. We look forward to collaborating with you! DISCLAIMER This announcement is for planning and market research purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation, request for proposal, request for quotation, or commitment by the Government. Participation in this event is voluntary and at no cost to the Government. The Government will not reimburse any costs associated with participation. Information exchanged during this event may be used by USACE to inform future acquisition strategies, project delivery approaches, and solicitation development; however, no procurement decisions will be made as a result of this event.

title: Borough of Millvale, Pennsylvania, Local Protection Project (LPP) PL84-99 Rehabilitation
description: The Millvale LPP was constructed by U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) in 1980 under the authority of Section 205 of the Flood Control Act of 1948 as amended. The project consists of about 6,200 feet of channel improvement including concrete gravity retaining walls, concrete wall supports, anchored concrete toe blocks, concrete cap walls, stone-filled gabion mattresses, flap gates and access ramps. The LPP is an urban Flood Control Work (FCW), and it is not a multipurpose project. Heavy rains from 1-12 April 2024 caused flooding which damaged the Project within Girtys Run, including bank erosion, shoaling, erosion of the improved channel, ruptured gabion baskets, washed-out concrete buttresses, and erosion of grouted riprap. Of particular concern are the washed-out buttresses which have migrated to the center of the improved channel, impeding streamflow. If the buttresses are not removed and stream bank improvements continue to deteriorate, there is a risk that debris will continue to accumulate and could ultimately damage the channel downstream of the impediment. To address these damages, Allegheny County requested rehabilitation assistance from USACE through the PL 84-99 program, which authorizes USACE to rehabilitate eligible Federal and non-Federal LPPs damaged or destroyed by floods. An agreement was signed on 6 August 2025 between the Borough of Millvale and USACE to complete the necessary repairs. The work is to be completed within 365 calendar days after written Notice to Proceed (NTP). The Anticipated Construction Cost is between $300,000.00 and $350,000.00. The North American Industrial Classification Code (NAICS) is 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The Small Business Size Standard is $45,000,000.00. Any resultant award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Purchase Order. The anticipated award date is 22 December 2026. The basis of award will be of best value to the Government. Quotes will be evaluated in accordance with (IAW) RFO Part 13 and 36, price and past performance. The Government reserves the right to reject any quotes that exceed available funds for this requirement. Information regarding the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers process for settling requests for equitable adjustments and duration goals to achieve definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts can be found by going to https://www.usace.army.mil/Strategic-Partnerships/Partnering/mod/129895/details/443/ then scrolling down on right hand side of page by clicking on View FFP Contract Changes Playbook Here.

The project consists of roadway and bridge maintenance at Thomas Edison National Historical Park (EDIS), Fort McHenry National Monument and Historic Shrine (FOMC), Steamtown National Historic Site (STEA), and Upper Delaware Scenic and Recreational River (UPDE). description: Sealed bids from certified Small Business Concerns only will be accepted for the Northeast Region Pavement and Bridge Preservation Construction, Project NP NER PMS BMS FY25(2), Solicitation Number 693C73-27-B-000004, located in Essex County, New Jersey; Pike, Wayne, and Lackawanna Counties, Pennsylvania; and the City of Baltimore, Maryland. The project consists of roadway and bridge maintenance at Thomas Edison National Historical Park (EDIS), Fort McHenry National Monument and Historic Shrine (FOMC), Steamtown National Historic Site (STEA), and Upper Delaware Scenic and Recreational River (UPDE). Proposal Volume III, Past Performance is requested two (2) weeks early on November 24, 2026, but not officially due until the proposal submittal date. Offerors are encouraged to submit questions as soon as possible for consideration. Questions shall be submitted using the Template for Submission of Comments in the �Attachments� section below. title: Repair Aids to Navigation (ATON) - Southern Area of USCG District Northeast
description: Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, transportation, supervision and disposal required for the structural repair, recapitalization, and/or demolish Aids to Navigation (ATON) structures at various southern sites in the CG Northeast District. The project consists of a Base Bid at the following sites in New York, Connecticut and Rhode Island: 1. New Haven Middle Breakwater West End Light (LLNR 24070): Replace existing tower in kind. 2. Stonington Outer Breakwater Light 4 (LLNR 20170): Replace existing concrete foundation, replace existing tower with standard 5x5 tower. 3. Stonington Breakwater Light 5 (LLNR 20175): Replace existing concrete foundation, repoint existing granite block foundation, replace existing tower in kind. 4. Norwalk Channel Light 10 (LLNR 24990): Replace existing foundation and tower in kind. 5. Port Jefferson West Breakwater Light 2A (LLNR 26145): Replace existing foundation and tower in kind. 6. Connecticut River Light 135 (LLNR 23300): Demolish ATON structure to below-grade elevation & reseed. 7. Point Judith Harbor of Refuge West Entrance Light 3 (LLNR 19505):Demolish existing structure & rebuild as standard 5x5 tower on concrete foundation offset from jetty erosion. An option item for an additional Aid to Navigation (ATON) structure repair in Massachusetts is included as follows: 1. Chatham Light (LLNR 525): Replace windows in kind & clean/recoat exterior/interior. The estimated value of the procurement is between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. A 20% bid guarantee is required. Performance and Payment bonds will be required. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction with a small business size standard of $45.0 million. Solicitation packages will be available on or about 4 November 2026. The tentative date set for receipt of bids is 8 December 2026 at 2:00 p.m. The base performance period is estimated to be 300 calendar days from issuance of Notice to Proceed and the option performance period is estimated to be 60 calendar days to be exercised at the Contracting Officers discretion. This acquisition is issued pursuant to FAR Part 14 Sealed Bidding and is 100% Set-Aside for Small Business concerns. All relevant solicitation documents, including specifications and drawings may be accessed for download beginning on the date of issue of the IFB at the following site: https://www.sam.gov. Vendors MUST be registered in the System for Award Management database through https://www.sam.gov in order to receive a federal government contract. THE GOVERNMENT RESERVES THE RIGHT TO CANCEL THIS SOLICITATION EITHER BEFORE OR AFTER THE CLOSING DATE. NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO THIS PRESOLICITATION NOTICE OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION REQUEST.

title: 2027 NIAID DMID Omnibus Broad Agency Announcement: Development of Medical Interventions for Infectious Diseases
description: INTRODUCTION: The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), one of 27 institutes of the NIH, an agency within the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS); conducts and supports research to understand, treat, and ultimately prevent the myriad infectious, immunologic, and allergic diseases that threaten the health and longevity of human lives.Through a variety of research grants and contracts, NIAID�s Division of Microbiology and Infectious Diseases (DMID) specifically supports extramural research to develop new medical interventions against infectious disease threats to include drug-resistant pathogens. NIAID/DMID intends to use this BAA to help address goals articulated in a number of strategic plans, such as in the Public Health Emergency Medical Countermeasures Enterprise Strategy and Implementation Plan (https://aspr.hhs.gov/PHEMCE/2024-PHEMCE-SIP/Pages/default.aspx), as well as current prioritized antimicrobial resistant threats identified by national death and infection estimates as determined by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention�s (CDC) to prevent and control antimicrobial resistance (https://www.cdc.gov/antimicrobial-resistance/data-research/threats/index.html). In addition, NIAID/DMID intends to use this BAA to encourage projects that align with the NIH priorities of enhancing rigor & reproducibility, improving biosafety and biosecurity, and the use of complementary non-animal testing methods where appropriate. This Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) is soliciting proposals to advance the research and development of promising candidate therapeutics, vaccines, and diagnostics for infectious diseases in each of three (3) Research Areas described below and more thoroughly discussed in the attached BAA Solicitation. An offeror should carefully review the content of the BAA Solicitation No. HHS-NIH-NIAID-BAA2026-1 for the comprehensive information regarding all requirements, the technical objective of each Research Area of this BAA Solicitation, instructions regarding the proposal submission, and a description of the evaluation and award process. Please note, due to the competitive nature of the BAA Solicitation, the NIAID is unable to offer advice or feedback regarding an offeror�s specific technical approach. Offerors should exercise their professional judgment when compiling their proposals in line with the requirements and specifications of the BAA Solicitation. Research Area 001 - Vaccine Candidates: The objective is to develop vaccine candidates through an early phase clinical trial that use a needle free (i.e., alternative to classical needle and syringe, see below for description) route of delivery to protect against infections caused by viral pathogens that include but are not limited to respiratory and vector borne viruses. The scope of this vaccine research area includes the preclinical development of a needle free vaccine candidate, IND enabling studies, limited process development, Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) compliant manufacturing, regulatory submissions to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and conduct of a Phase 1 or early Phase 2 clinical trial. The scope of work must include a clinical trial. Offerors must propose a single vaccine candidate for protection against a specific viral pathogen. The vaccine candidate may provide a breadth of protection against other viral strains or viruses. A strong justification is required to support (1) the proposed vaccine antigen and platform for the disease indication, (2) the use of a clinically relevant adjuvant (if needed), and (3) a clinically relevant needle free route of delivery. Research Area 002 - Therapeutic Candidates: The objective is to develop safe, effective, new therapeutic products that will improve patient outcomes against serious infectious diseases for which there are no approved therapeutics, or for those that are refractory to treatment despite appropriate antimicrobial therapy or due to pathogen resistance. Infectious diseases caused by the following viruses, bacteria and fungi pathogens are targeted: Viral hemorrhagic fever viruses (e.g., EBOV, SUDV, MARV, LASV, hantavirus) https://www.cdc.gov/viral-hemorrhagic-fevers/about/index.html Encephalitic paramyxoviruses (e.g. hendra virus, nipah virus) Picornaviruses (broad spectrum approaches that include EV68, EV70 and coxsackie virus) At least two of the following (i.e., addressed with a broad spectrum antimicrobial): susceptible and carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE), susceptible and multidrug resistant (MDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and susceptible and Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter (CRAB), with potential to improve patient outcomes in the clinic; Candida auris, Cryptococcus spp., Aspergillus fumigatus, and/or Mucorales Adjunct medical interventions to support or enhance effectiveness of antimicrobial agents to address underlying pathology that is not resolved after clearance of pathogens, may be considered. Important notice to Offerors: For this Research Area, �therapeutic� activity means curing disease by eliminating or substantially reducing infective pathogens by administering antimicrobial pharmaceutical agents, with or without a host-directed therapy. Additionally, proposed therapeutic products should consider the impact on a healthy microbiome. Preventative treatments are not included in the scope of this Research Area. A therapeutic candidate refers to an advanced lead series, preclinical candidates, or a clinical candidate, that is a new chemical entity. This includes small molecules, natural products, nucleosides, or peptides of </= 40 amino acids, monoclonal antibodies, nanobodies, nanobody conjugate/fusion products, microbiome-based therapeutics or bacteriophages. Research Area 002 will support lead optimization, pre-clinical Investigational New Drug (IND) enabling studies, and Phase 1 clinical trials (or proof of concept Phase 2 clinical trials) of lead candidates with demonstrated therapeutic activities. This includes support for traditional, novel (e.g., small molecules) and non-traditional (e.g., including but not limited to phage, and host-directed) therapeutics for infectious diseases where patients lack effective interventions, as well as therapeutics that promote host-mediated resolution of disease. The scope of support differs depending on the developmental stage of the project being proposed, which is further discussed in the BAA Solicitation. Research Area 003 - In Vitro Diagnostics The objective of Research Area 003 is to develop innovative, technology platforms that will speed detection and identification of infectious viruses covering a broad panel of virus families, including viruses causing acute infections as well as those causing chronic infections. Technology platform innovation to achieve faster actionable sequencing results (approaching 2 hr) direct from primary clinical specimens, as well as more accessible workflow and configuration (i.e., point-of-care) are preferred. Furthermore, full sample-to-answer platform solutions are preferred. The system should accept specimen volumes from 0.5 to 5 milliliters (mL). The system should include nearly full automation (little or no hands-on activity after specimen has been loaded into system). Sample preparation components of the system should yield sufficient analyte recovery from a starting titer of 10-100 genomic copies per mL of biofluid for downstream analysis, including detection, identification, and characterization of the nucleic acid material. Innovations during platform development might include, for example: Automated sample prep for high recovery from low pathogen load. Faster specimen-to-answer for total test time <2 hours. Broad viral pathogen detection capability, covering one or more members of the priority pathogen families (see below). title: Preventive Maintenance and Repair Services - Kahuku Training Area (KTA)
description: The Regional Contracting Office Hawaii (RCO-HI) has a requirement for preventive maintenance, inspection, testing, unscheduled assessment/trouble-call, and repair services for HVAC; fire alarm and mass notification; emergency lighting and exit signs; and lightning protection systems at Kahuku Training Area, Oahu, Hawaii. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, transportation, supervision, and other resources necessary to perform the requirement in accordance with the solicitation and Performance Work Statement. This solicitation is issued as Request for Quotations (RFQ) No. W912CN27QA008 and is a 100 percent Total Small Business Set-Aside under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 561210. The Government contemplates award of one firm-fixed-price requirements contract consisting of a base period and four 12-month option periods, with evaluation of the six-month option to extend services under FAR 52.217-8. The solicitation is conducted under the provisions of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. To be eligible for award, quoters must maintain an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM), including current and complete representations and certifications, at the time of quote submission and at the time of award. Quoters are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for amendments and other solicitation information through the closing date. Refer to Section L, pages 113�116, for quote-submission instructions and required submission content, and Section M, pages 120�121, for evaluation criteria. Quoters must submit all required documents, including the signed SF 1449 and acknowledgement of all amendments, completed pricing documents for all applicable priced CLINs, and the technical capability submission. Do not price Repair Services CLIN 0006 or its option-year counterparts; repair services will be ordered and priced after award through Contracting Officer-issued firm-fixed-price task orders. Written questions are due no later than 10:00 a.m. Hawaii Standard Time (HST), Thursday, 19 November 2026. Questions shall be submitted to both: Travis Tonini, Contract Specialist: travis.c.tonini.civ@army.mil Keely K. Pool, Contracting Officer: keely.k.pool.civ@army.mil Completed quotations and all supporting documentation must be submitted electronically by email to Travis Tonini at travis.c.tonini.civ@army.mil no later than 10:00 a.m. HST, Tuesday, 8 December 2026. Faxed quotations will not be accepted. A site visit at Kahuku Training Area is scheduled for Tuesday, 17 November 2026. Attendance is strongly encouraged but not mandatory. Offerors intending to attend must submit required visit-request information no later than 12:00 p.m. HST, Tuesday, 10 November 2026, to Travis Tonini for further instructions. (Solit file states 10:00 AM, but 12:00 p.m. is the official cut off).

title: ERDC Watercraft and Ship Simulator Support Services Multiple Award Task Order Contract
description: This is an unrestricted, full and open, Request for Proposal for the establishment of a Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC).The ordering period will consist of a 24-month base period and three 12-month option periods, for a total potential ordering period of 60 months, if all options are exercised. The overall objective of this procurement is to augment ERDCs ship simulation capabilities by acquiring specialized, independent maritime simulation and engineering support services to deliver technically rigorous, time-sensitive simulation solutions to USACE navigation challenges. The Contractor shall independently execute designated simulation tasks, conduct technical analyses, and deliver finalized engineering reports as specified in individual Task Orders, leveraging external maritime expertise to support the USACE navigation mission. Navigation study services not directly connected with project maintenance and operations are considered commercial activities and not inherently governmental. (33 U.S.C. 2321(b)).

title: Greece – Heating oil – ΠΡΟΜΗΘΕΙΑ ΠΕΤΡΕΛΑΙΟΥ ΘΕΡΜΑΝΣΗΣ 2027-2028
description: Η μελέτη αυτή αφορά την ΠΡΟΜΗΘΕΙΑ ΠΕΤΡΕΛΑΙΟΥ ΘΕΡΜΑΝΣΗΣ 2027-2028 για τις ανάγκες του Δήμου ΝΕΑΣ ΠΡΟΠΟΝΤΙΔΑΣ για διάστημα δύο ετών και θα χρηματοδοτηθεί από ιδίους πόρους Τα υπό προμήθεια καύσιμα θέρμανσης πρέπει να έχουν τις προδιαγραφές που ορίζει το Ανώτατο Χημικό Συμβούλιο του Γενικού Χημείου του Κράτους σύμφωνα με τα ΦΕΚ 410/11-4-2001 και 872/4-6-2007 και θα πρέπει να είναι σύμφωνες με αυτές των ελληνικών διυλιστηρίων και ποιότητας όμοιας με εκείνη που παράγουν τα διυλιστήρια στην χώρα μας. Σε καμιά περίπτωση δεν επιτρέπεται η ύπαρξη ακαθαρσιών, χρώματος ή άλλων ξένων στοιχείων. Ο Δήμος διατηρεί το δικαίωμα να αποστέλλει δείγματα από τα καύσιμα ώστε να ελέγχεται τόσο η ποιότητα όσο και το αν πληρούν τις απαιτούμενες προδιαγραφές στο Γενικό Χημείο του Κράτους. Τα παραπάνω στοιχεία θεωρούνται ουσιώδη και απαράβατα εκτός αν αναφέρεται ότι αποτελούν προτίμηση ή επιθυμία της υπηρεσίας. Τα προς προμήθεια είδη κατατάσσονται στους ακόλουθους κωδικούς του Κοινού Λεξιλογίου δημοσίων συμβάσεων CPV: 09135100-5 (πετρέλαιο θέρμανσης), Η ενδεικτική δαπάνη της προμήθειας προϋπολογίζεται στο ποσό των 1.170.237,60 € (943.740,00 € πλέον ΦΠΑ) Η εκτέλεση της προμήθειας θα γίνει σύμφωνα με τον Ν.4412/2016(ΦΕΚ147/8-8-2016) και τον Ν.3852/2010(ΦΕΚ87/7-6-2010). Η διάρκεια της σύμβασης θα είναι για δύο έτη και μετά από σύμφωνη γνώμη και των δύο συμβαλλόμενων δύναται να παραταθεί έως δυο έτη το ανώτερο, προκειμένου να καλυφθούν τρέχουσες ανάγκες του Δήμου, χωρίς τροποποίηση της συμβατικής αξίας. Η σύμβαση δεν χωρίζεται σε τμήματα διότι αφορά σε ένα είδος με διαφορετικούς κωδικούς στον προϋπολογισμό του Δήμου. Επίσης οι ποσότητες είναι ενδεικτικές. Εφόσον υπάρξει μία σύμβαση, μπορούν να γίνουν επουσιώδεις τροποποιήσεις και αυξομειώσεις ποσοτήτων μέσα στην ίδια σύμβαση, οπότε να μπορέσουμε να αξιοποιήσουμε όλες τις ποσότητες και να εξυπηρετηθούν όλες οι ευαίσθητες δομές του Δήμου. Η σύμβαση θα ανατεθεί με το κριτήριο της πλέον συμφέρουσας από οικονομική άποψη προσφοράς, βάσει τιμής και συγκεκριμένα: Κριτήριο βάσει τιμής για τα καύσιμα (χαμηλότερη τιμή), θεωρείται το μεγαλύτερο ποσοστό έκπτωσης επί τοις εκατό (%), στη νόμιμα διαμορφούμενη μέση τιμή πώλησης εκάστου είδους, την ημέρα παράδοσης τους, του Παρατηρητηρίου Τιμών Υγρών Καυσίμων του Υπουργείου Ανάπτυξης και Ανταγωνιστικότητας για το νομό Χαλκιδικής.

title: GPS Ground Segment Monitor Station Service (MSS)
description: Section 1: General Information Pursuant to Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 15.101(c), this is a Sources Sought Notice/ Request for Information (RFI) only. This notice is issued solely for conducting market research and planning purposes in accordance with RFO Part 10 and RFO Part 5. This announcement is for Market Research only and does not constitute a commitment, promise, or obligation by the Government to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or solicitation of any kind. The Government will not award a contract based on responses to this notice. The Space Force Portfolio Acquisition Executive (SFPAE) for Satellite Communications and Positioning, Navigation and Timing (SATCOM and PNT) is not seeking proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals. Respondents are advised that the Government will not pay for any information, bid preparation costs, or administrative expenses incurred in responding to this notice. Acquisition Attribute Program Baseline Details Notice ID / Solicitation Number SSC-GCS-MSS-SSN-2026 Sponsoring Agency / Office United States Space Force (USSF) / Space Systems Command (SSC) / MD31 Product Service Code (PSC) 1677 (Space Vehicle Remote Control Systems) North American Industry Classification (NAICS) 541715 (Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)) Classification & Security Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) / SECRET Facility Clearance Required Response Date & Time 8 December 2026 at 3:00 PM MST Primary Points of Contact Mr. Daniel Hilger, Procuring Contracting Officer (PCO) Mr. Carl Griffin, Civil Navigation (CNAV) Project Lead Section 2: System Background & Scope of Work 2.1 Background The USSF is actively modernizing the GPS Ground Control Segment (GCS) to deliver enhanced Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) resilience and operationalize modernized civil and military signals. As part of this effort, USSF seeks to address necessary sustainment and modernization of its global PNT ground receiver network. The legacy ground control segment, the Architecture Evolution Plan (AEP), receives real-time tracking data from a total of 17 global monitor stations, 11 of which are estimated to face obsolescence in late 2028. USSF seeks options to transition to a modernized, sustainable ground segment architecture to maintain AEP's clock and orbit estimation engine (the Kalman Filter). To that end, the Government is requesting interested respondents submit statements of capability (SOCs) describing potential solutions to provide the capabilities described herein. Furthermore, the Space Force requires that any replacement ground receiver infrastructure not merely duplicate legacy capabilities but simultaneously address broader enterprise needs. The replacement architecture must serve as the primary operational enabler for: Civil Navigation (CNAV) Modernization: Providing independent, continuous signal-in-space tracking, integrity monitoring, and safety-of-life assurance for advanced civilian signals (L2C, L5, L1C) to support joint Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and international civil aviation commitments. Military Navigation (MNAV) & M-Code Operations: Integrating secure, high-fidelity tracking of military M-Code signals to enable robust anti-jam, anti-spoof Navigation Warfare (NAVWAR) operations and Regional Military Protection (RMP). 2.2 Spectrum & Signal Tracking Requirements To demonstrate that the required monitoring capability extends beyond legacy single-frequency L-Band observables, the proposed Monitor Station Service (MSS) must provide simultaneous multi-frequency, multi-code tracking across a growing constellation (up to 63 Space Vehicles). The solution must provide continuous tracking, measurement extraction, and observable processing across the following specific signal tiers: Signal Tier Frequency / Signal Type Capabilities & Processing Requirements Legacy Signals (Baseline Parity) L1 (1575.42 MHz): L1P-codeless L1 C/A, L1P(Y) L2 (1227.60 MHz): L2P(Y) L2P-codless Continuous tracking, legacy LNAV message demodulation, pseudorange/carrier-phase measurement extraction, and legacy telemetry processing for core AEP Kalman Filter orbit/clock estimation continuity. Modernized Civil Signals (CNAV) L5 (1176.45 MHz): Safety-of-Life (SoL), L5I,L5Q L2 (1227.46 MHz): L2C (L2CM,L2CL) L1 (1575.42 MHz): L1C (L1CD,L1CP) CNAV message demodulation, multi-frequency ionospheric delay cancellation, advanced signal quality monitoring (SQM), interference/jamming detection, and civil aviation safety-of-life (SoL) processing standards to support L5 Initial Operational Capability (IOC). Military Signals (Modernized) L1 / L2 M-Code (1575.42 MHz / 1227.46 MHz): Earth Coverage & Regional Military Protection (RMP) Direct M-Code acquisition and tracking, cryptographic channel decoding via NSA-certified security architecture, advanced anti-jam / anti-spoof protections, and Modernized User Equipment (MGUE) warfighter operational support. 2.3 Core Capabilities & Scope of Work The scope of this market research centers on identifying industry capabilities and realistic timelines to deliver an integrated, secure, and safety-certified Monitor Station Service (MSS) that interfaces seamlessly with AEP and external mission partners (FAA, NGA). The Government intends to acquire and take delivery of the software baseline and associated technical data rights to ensure long-term organic C2 baseline control and sustainment within the Government boundary. The Government is seeking responses that demonstrate capability across the following core technical tasks: Integrated Multi-Signal Ingestion: Acquire, process, format, and distribute raw binary and smoothed pseudorange, carrier phase, Accumulated Delta Range (ADR), and Signal Quality Metrics (SQM) across all legacy, CNAV, and MNAV signals listed in Section 2.2. Modular API & Service-Oriented Integration: Expose receiver monitoring and control capabilities through a Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) utilizing standardized Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) and messaging layers to decouple data feeds from underlying receiver hardware. Safety-of-Life Signal Assurance: Support rigorous software design assurance standards (certifiable up to Design Assurance Level D / DAL D per RTCA DO-278A / DO-178C) to provide real-time signal deformation detection, Code Carrier Coherence (CCC), and anomalous event alerting. Cryptographic & Boundary Security: Provide NSA-approved cryptographic handling capabilities for military key management, secure unclassified/classified cross-domain boundary routing, and continuous Risk Management Framework (RMF) security control validation in a secure government cloud/on-prem environment (IL5/IL6) to maintain an active DoD Authority to Operate (ATO). Receiver Security Certification (FSET): Provide receiver hardware, software, and firmware capable of achieving or maintaining security certification through the Space Systems Command (SSC) Functional Security Engineering Team (FSET) for deployment across global, unclassified, and collateral Secret monitoring locations, including supporting delta FSET recertification processes for component and cryptographic updates. Section 3: Information Requested from Industry To assist the government in conducting its statutory market research, all respondents are requested to organize their capability statements into the following structured sections: Part A: Corporate Profile Administrative Details: Company Name, Mailing Address, CAGE code, and Unique Entity ID (UEI). title: GPS Ground Segment Monitor Station Service (MSS)
description: Section 1: General Information Pursuant to Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 15.101(c), this is a Sources Sought Notice/ Request for Information (RFI) only. This notice is issued solely for conducting market research and planning purposes in accordance with RFO Part 10 and RFO Part 5. This announcement is for Market Research only and does not constitute a commitment, promise, or obligation by the Government to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or solicitation of any kind. The Government will not award a contract based on responses to this notice. The Space Force Portfolio Acquisition Executive (SFPAE) for Satellite Communications and Positioning, Navigation and Timing (SATCOM and PNT) is not seeking proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals. Respondents are advised that the Government will not pay for any information, bid preparation costs, or administrative expenses incurred in responding to this notice. Acquisition Attribute Program Baseline Details Notice ID / Solicitation Number SSC-GCS-MSS-SSN-2026 Sponsoring Agency / Office United States Space Force (USSF) / Space Systems Command (SSC) / MD31 Product Service Code (PSC) 1677 (Space Vehicle Remote Control Systems) North American Industry Classification (NAICS) 541715 (Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)) Classification & Security Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) / SECRET Facility Clearance Required Response Date & Time 8 December 2026 at 3:00 PM MST Primary Points of Contact Mr. Daniel Hilger, Procuring Contracting Officer (PCO) Mr. Carl Griffin, Civil Navigation (CNAV) Project Lead Section 2: System Background & Scope of Work 2.1 Background The USSF is actively modernizing the GPS Ground Control Segment (GCS) to deliver enhanced Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) resilience and operationalize modernized civil and military signals. As part of this effort, USSF seeks to address necessary sustainment and modernization of its global PNT ground receiver network. The legacy ground control segment, the Architecture Evolution Plan (AEP), receives real-time tracking data from a total of 17 global monitor stations, 11 of which are estimated to face obsolescence in late 2028. USSF seeks options to transition to a modernized, sustainable ground segment architecture to maintain AEP's clock and orbit estimation engine (the Kalman Filter). To that end, the Government is requesting interested respondents submit statements of capability (SOCs) describing potential solutions to provide the capabilities described herein. Furthermore, the Space Force requires that any replacement ground receiver infrastructure not merely duplicate legacy capabilities but simultaneously address broader enterprise needs. The replacement architecture must serve as the primary operational enabler for: Civil Navigation (CNAV) Modernization: Providing independent, continuous signal-in-space tracking, integrity monitoring, and safety-of-life assurance for advanced civilian signals (L2C, L5, L1C) to support joint Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and international civil aviation commitments. Military Navigation (MNAV) & M-Code Operations: Integrating secure, high-fidelity tracking of military M-Code signals to enable robust anti-jam, anti-spoof Navigation Warfare (NAVWAR) operations and Regional Military Protection (RMP). 2.2 Spectrum & Signal Tracking Requirements To demonstrate that the required monitoring capability extends beyond legacy single-frequency L-Band observables, the proposed Monitor Station Service (MSS) must provide simultaneous multi-frequency, multi-code tracking across a growing constellation (up to 63 Space Vehicles). The solution must provide continuous tracking, measurement extraction, and observable processing across the following specific signal tiers: Signal Tier Frequency / Signal Type Capabilities & Processing Requirements Legacy Signals (Baseline Parity) L1 (1575.42 MHz): L1P-codeless L1 C/A, L1P(Y) L2 (1227.60 MHz): L2P(Y) L2P-codless Continuous tracking, legacy LNAV message demodulation, pseudorange/carrier-phase measurement extraction, and legacy telemetry processing for core AEP Kalman Filter orbit/clock estimation continuity. Modernized Civil Signals (CNAV) L5 (1176.45 MHz): Safety-of-Life (SoL), L5I,L5Q L2 (1227.46 MHz): L2C (L2CM,L2CL) L1 (1575.42 MHz): L1C (L1CD,L1CP) CNAV message demodulation, multi-frequency ionospheric delay cancellation, advanced signal quality monitoring (SQM), interference/jamming detection, and civil aviation safety-of-life (SoL) processing standards to support L5 Initial Operational Capability (IOC). Military Signals (Modernized) L1 / L2 M-Code (1575.42 MHz / 1227.46 MHz): Earth Coverage & Regional Military Protection (RMP) Direct M-Code acquisition and tracking, cryptographic channel decoding via NSA-certified security architecture, advanced anti-jam / anti-spoof protections, and Modernized User Equipment (MGUE) warfighter operational support. 2.3 Core Capabilities & Scope of Work The scope of this market research centers on identifying industry capabilities and realistic timelines to deliver an integrated, secure, and safety-certified Monitor Station Service (MSS) that interfaces seamlessly with AEP and external mission partners (FAA, NGA). The Government intends to acquire and take delivery of the software baseline and associated technical data rights to ensure long-term organic C2 baseline control and sustainment within the Government boundary. The Government is seeking responses that demonstrate capability across the following core technical tasks: Integrated Multi-Signal Ingestion: Acquire, process, format, and distribute raw binary and smoothed pseudorange, carrier phase, Accumulated Delta Range (ADR), and Signal Quality Metrics (SQM) across all legacy, CNAV, and MNAV signals listed in Section 2.2. Modular API & Service-Oriented Integration: Expose receiver monitoring and control capabilities through a Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) utilizing standardized Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) and messaging layers to decouple data feeds from underlying receiver hardware. Safety-of-Life Signal Assurance: Support rigorous software design assurance standards (certifiable up to Design Assurance Level D / DAL D per RTCA DO-278A / DO-178C) to provide real-time signal deformation detection, Code Carrier Coherence (CCC), and anomalous event alerting. Cryptographic & Boundary Security: Provide NSA-approved cryptographic handling capabilities for military key management, secure unclassified/classified cross-domain boundary routing, and continuous Risk Management Framework (RMF) security control validation in a secure government cloud/on-prem environment (IL5/IL6) to maintain an active DoD Authority to Operate (ATO). Receiver Security Certification (FSET): Provide receiver hardware, software, and firmware capable of achieving or maintaining security certification through the Space Systems Command (SSC) Functional Security Engineering Team (FSET) for deployment across global, unclassified, and collateral Secret monitoring locations, including supporting delta FSET recertification processes for component and cryptographic updates. Section 3: Information Requested from Industry To assist the government in conducting its statutory market research, all respondents are requested to organize their capability statements into the following structured sections: Part A: Corporate Profile Administrative Details: Company Name, Mailing Address, CAGE code, and Unique Entity ID (UEI). Socioeconomic Status: State your business size and any applicable socioeconomic designations under NAICS 541715 (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB, etc.). Facility Clearance: Confirm whether your company possesses an active, DOD-approved SECRET Facility Clearance (required for ground segment integration testing an

title: Electron Storage Ring D2 Dipole Magnets
description: Brookhaven Science Associates, LLC (BSA), under a Prime Contract for the operation of Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL) with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), herewith solicits your proposal for 195 EIC ESR D2 Dipole Magnets (194 production magnets and 1 first article magnet). The scope of this acquisition comprises of the detailed magnet engineering design and production of Electron Storage Ring (ESR) D2 Dipole Magnets for the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC). The magnets are an integral part of the process to create intense beams of relativistic energy electrons and ions in opposing particle storage rings that will be brought into collision in a large experimental detector. This will provide insight into the internal structure of protons and neutrons and the gluelike force that holds them together. The Offeror shall furnish all labor, services, materials and equipment in accordance with the draft contract, Enclosure 1, including the Statement of Work and referenced Specifications and Drawings. Please submit your proposal by 5:00PM EST on December 8, 2026. All questions must be submitted in writing via e-mail; replies to questions will be provided in writing and, if considered to be of general interest, will be transmitted to all other offerors. If for any reason you are unable to submit a proposal, kindly reply in writing and return this letter with all of the attachments. Sincerely, Cindy Blanchard Senior Contracts Specialist Procurement & Property Management Division Brookhaven National Laboratory Upton, New York 11973 Phone: (631) 344-5770 Email: cblanchar@bnl.gov

title: Indkøb af leverandører til undervisning og mentoring på forløbet "Fra ide til forretning"
description: Erhvervshusenes brede iværksætterindsats søger en leverandør til at gennemføre 8 udgaver af inkubationsforløbet Fra idé til forretning med opstart i 2027 med mulighed for tilkøb af yderligere 8 forløb i 2028 (se nærmere længere nede). Inkubationsforløbet består af tre workshops samt mentoring efter hver workshop. Målet er at give ambitiøse og motiverede iværksættere på idé-stadiet værktøjerne til at bygge virksomhed. Vi modtager ofte mange kvalificerede tilbud. Læs derfor venligst nedenstående grundigt, inden du indsender et tilbud. Opgaven Erhvervshusene driver, som en del af Virksomhedsudvikling Danmark, inkubationsforløbet ”Fra idé til forretning”. Det er et forløb målrettet iværksættere, der er motiverede og ambitiøse, og ønsker at omsætte deres idé/projekt til en levedygtig og skalerbar forretningsmodel. ”Fra idé til forretning” består af tre workshops, som gennemføres over ca. fem uger med ca. 2 uger mellem hver workshop: Modul 1: Kick-off – hvilket problem løser du og for hvem? Modul 2: Hvorfor skal kunden vælge din løsning? Modul 3: Salg – hvordan kommer du ud til dine kunder? Efter hver workshop skal iværksætterne tilbydes mentoring (se nærmere længere nede). Efter workshop 3 får deltagerne mulighed for at pitche foran et panel og få yderligere feedback på deres forretningsmodel. Panelet arrangeres og håndteres i samarbejde med Connect Denmark. Vi søger en partner, der kan gennemføre hele forløbet inkl. facilitering, undervisning og mentoring. Vi vil herunder beskrive indholdet af de enkelte workshops, som en leverandør skal kunne levere på.

title: Germany – Architectural, engineering and planning services – JG | U Ersatzneubauten Gewächshäuser - Generalplanervergabe
description: Für die Baumaßnahme "Ersatzneubauten Gewächshäuser" in Mainz werden Generalplanerleistungen für die abschnittsweise Umsetzung des Vorhabens vergeben. Gegenstand sind der Rückbau der be-stehenden Gewächshausanlagen sowie die Planung und Realisierung der Ersatzneubauten ein-schließlich der zugehörigen Freianlagen und der Einbindung in das Gesamtareal des Botanischen Gartens. Der Generalplaner übernimmt die übergeordnete Koordination, Integration und Schnittstellenbear-beitung der beauftragten Objekt- und Fachplanungen sowie die Einbindung der vom Auftraggeber gesondert beauftragten Fachbeteiligten. Die Planung erfolgt bis zur ausführungsreifen und vergabe-fähigen Planung einschließlich Leistungsbeschreibungen und Leistungsverzeichnissen. Seitens des Auftraggebers wird eine gebündelte Vergabe wesentlicher Bauleistungen an einen Generalunter-nehmer favorisiert. Besonders zu berücksichtigen sind der laufende Pflanzen-, Forschungs- und Gar-tenbetrieb sowie die abschnittsweise und teilweise überlappende Umsetzung der Bauabschnitte. Der Leistungsumfang umfasst insbesondere: - Objektplanung Gebäude und Innenräume: Grundleistungen der LPH 2 bis 9 sowie die projektspezifischen Besonderen Leistungen gem. Teil 3 Abschnitt 1 HOAI. - Tragwerksplanung: Grundleistungen der LPH 1 bis 6 sowie ergänzende Besondere Leistungen für Vergabe, Ausführung, ingenieurtechnische Kontrolle, Dokumentation und Objektbetreuung gem. Teil 4 Abschnitt 1 HOAI. - Thermische Bauphysik / Wärmeschutz / Energiebilanzierung: Grundleistungen der LPH 1 bis 7 nach Anlage 1 Nr. 1.2 HOAI sowie die projektspezifischen Besonderen Leistungen, insbesondere zu Wärme-, Feuchte-, Kondensat- und Wärmebrückenschutz sowie zu den Schnittstellen der Gewächshaushülle zur TGA. - Freianlagenplanung: Grundleistungen der LPH 2 bis 9 sowie die projektspezifischen Besonderen Leistungen einschließlich Erschließung, Vegetation, Bauabschnitts- und Interimszuständen sowie Schnittstellen zu Regenwasserbewirtschaftung, technischen Außenanlagen und Entwässerung gem. Teil 3 Abschnitt 2 i.V.m. Anlage 11 HOAI. - Technische Ausrüstung gem. Teil 4 Abschnitt 2 HOAI: Leistungen nach Maßgabe der jeweiligen spezifischen Leistungspflichten für - Anlagengruppen 1 bis 3 und 7, insbesondere gewächshausspezifische Klima-, Heizungs-, Lüf-tungs-, Bewässerungs-, Vernebelungs-, Verschattungs- und Energieschirmtechnik, - Anlagengruppen 4 und 5, insbesondere elektrotechnische sowie kommunikations- und infor-mationstechnische Anlagen, und - Anlagengruppe 8, Gebäudeautomation/Gebäudeleittechnik einschließlich Regelungs-, Steue-rungs-, Monitoring- und Schnittstellenfunktionen. Ergänzend sind Leistungen des bauordnungsrechtlichen Brandschutzes in Anlehnung an AHO-Heft Nr. 17, der Nachhaltigkeitskoordination / BNB gemäß projektspezifischer Zielvereinbarung sowie des Schadstoffmanagements, des selektiven Rückbaus, der Entsorgungs- und Materialstromplanung und des zirkulären Bauens gemäß den jeweiligen spezifischen Leistungspflichten zu erbringen. Die Leistungen werden entsprechend den dort festgelegten Leistungsstufen 1 bis 5 erbracht. Die Fachplanung Brandschutz orientiert sich an den Leistungsstufen des AHO-Heftes Nr. 17. Die Leistungen BNB/Nachhaltigkeitskoordination sowie Schadstoffe / zirkuläres Bauen werden projekt-spezifisch in Leistungsstufen 1 bis 5 gegliedert. Soweit einzelne Leistungen Leistungsphasen der HOAI zugeordnet sind, ergibt sich die jeweilige Zuordnung aus den spezifischen Leistungspflichten. Die Leistungen "Kunst am Bau" werden gesondert betrachtet. Die daraus resultierenden planeri-schen, baulichen, technischen und terminlichen Schnittstellen sind durch den Generalplaner in die Gesamtplanung und den Bauablauf zu integrieren; die fachlich-künstlerische Bewertung ist nicht Be-standteil der Generalplanerleistung. Vom Auftraggeber gesondert beauftragte bzw. bereitgestellte Leistungen - insbesondere Bau-grund/Geotechnik, Vermessung, SiGeKo, Ingenieur für kontaminierte Bereiche, übergeordnete brandschutztechnische Beratung/Prüfung, Prüfstatik, Kanal-/Leitungs- und Spartenuntersuchungen sowie Kampfmitteluntersuchungen - sind hinsichtlich ihrer für die Gesamtplanung relevanten Ergeb-nisse durch den Generalplaner zu integrieren. Die fachliche Verantwortung verbleibt bei den jeweili-gen Leistungserbringern.

title: Germany – Hospital facilities construction work – 111 Einrichtung für AEMP
description: Das Städtische Klinikum Kiel (SKK) soll im Zuge des Neubauvorhabens eine neue AEMP und eine neue Endoskopieaufbereitung erhalten. Beide Bereiche befinden sich im Sockelgeschoss des Haus 6. Ziel ist es ein gutes Gesamtkonzept für die Sterilgutaufbereitung zu implementieren. Der Leistungsumfang dieser Ausschreibung sieht die Lieferung, Montage und Inbetriebnahme folgender Geräte vor: Los 1: - 4 Dampfsterilisatoren (8StE, 9 StE oder 10 StE) it Entladesystem und mit 2 Elektrodampferzeugern - Trennwandelement mit Rückgabefenster (reiner /steriler Bereich) - Beschickungswagen -Wartung und Validierung Los2: - 2 große CWAs in der AEMP - 1 kleinere CWA in der Endoskopieaufbereitung, aufgrund der Raumgröße darf diese CWA nicht größer als 250x205cm (BxT) sein. - 5 bis 6 Durchreiche RDGs für die AEMP(die Ausschreibung ist hier bewusst konzeptionell offen gestaltet.) mit Durchreichefenster/Rückgabeschleuse - Automatisierungssystem im unreinen und im reinen Bereich (z.B. Rollenbahn, Roboter etc.) - 2 Durchreiche RDGs für die Aufbereitung von OP-Schuhen im 2.OG - 1 Zentrale Dosieranlage im Kellergeschoss mit Leitungen bis ins Sockelgeschoss. - Wartung und Validierung - Zubehörwagen Zu beachten ist, dass die Raumhöhe im Sockelgeschoss stark begrenzt ist. Die Raumhöhe (LRH) beträgt 2,35m und die Rohdeckenhöhe 3,06m. Es befindet sich eine hohe Installationsdichte der TGA in der Zwischendecke. Dadurch stehen im Deckenbereich nur ca. 10cm Deckenaufbau für die Installation zur Verfügung. Angestrebt wird ein mehrstufiges Verfahren. Im Teilnahmewettbewerb wird die allgemeine Eignung des Bieters geprüft und in der 2.Auswahlstufe des Teilnahmewettbewerbs wird eine losweise Eignung geprüft. Nach Durchlauf dieser Auswahlstufe wird pro Los die Bewerberzahl auf max. 3 Bieter reduziert (Bei gleicher Punktzahl entscheidet das Los). Die 3 Bieter aus Los 1 und die 3 Bieter aus Los 2 werden dann zur Angebotsabgabe aufgefordert. Nach der Angebotsphase folgen Verhandlungsgespräche mit den jeweiligen Bietern, die daraufhin die Möglichkeit haben, ein finales Angebot einzureichen.

title: Germany – Ventilation installation work – Grasweg 72-76 - Lüftung
description: SBH | Schulbau Hamburg hat als Landesbetrieb der Freien und Hansestadt Hamburg (nachstehend SBH genannt) die Aufgabe, die Schulimmobilien unter Berücksichtigung der schulischen Belange nach wirtschaftlichen Grundsätzen zu planen, zu bauen, zu unterhalten und zu bewirtschaften und die mehr als 400 Schulen an die Behörde für Schule und Berufsbildung (BSB) zu vermieten. --------------- Die Freie und Hansestadt Hamburg, vertreten durch SBH, plant die Heinrich-Hertz-Schule mit einem Neubau (Nutzung: Mensaflächen, Fachklass Musik, Fachklassen und allg. Unterrichtsräume) zu erweitern. Der neue Baukörper schließt westlich an die Bestandbibliothek an, ohne funktional über einen Durchgang mit ihr verbunden zu werden. Der Neubau stärkt das Bild der Schulstraße durch Anlehnung an den Bestand in Material, Anmut und Form. Der Haupteingang des Neubaus befindet sich eindeutig zentral unter dem dreigeschossigen Gebäudeteil. Ebenfalls im Bereich des Haupteingangs befindet sich ein zusätzlicher Nebeneingang, der es den Schülern ermöglicht auf kürzestem Weg in die Mensa zu gelangen. Die Mensaküche wird über den Zugang im Osten angeliefert. Die Anlieferung der Lebensmittel erfolgt mit Rollwagen über den Eingang auf der Ostseite, der mit einem Vordach versehen ist. Hier wird die Ware ausgepackt, kontrolliert und auf interne Behälter sortiert. Unterhalb des 3-Geschossers bildet sich eine großzügiger Rücksprung hin zum Schulhof, der als überdachte Pausenmöglichkeit genutzt werden kann. Im Erdgeschoss liegen zentral und schnell erreichbar die Mensa mit Küche und Kiosk, die Fachklassen und der Raum für Schüler und Lehrküche. Die Mensa ist eine Versammlungsstätte. Im 1.Obergeschoss befinden sich weitere Mensaflächen und Fachklassen mit entsprechenden Nebenräumen und Differenzierungsflächen. --------------- Hier: Lüftung --------------- Alle innenliegenden Räume im Bereich Schule werden über eine zentrale Lüftungsanlage angeschlossen. buyer: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
title: Germany – Foreign economic-aid-related services – 10043822-Implementation Support National Ecosystem Assessments in Saint Lucia and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
description: Caribbean ecosystems are exceptionally rich in biodiversity and provide essential services for climate resilience, economic activity and social development. However, biodiversity is declining due to resource overexploitation, habitat loss, unsustainable agriculture, pollution and climate change. Ecosystem values are often insufficiently reflected in decision-making, partly because national assessments and relevant data are lacking. Inclusive assessments are also needed to better understand how different groups, including women, young people, Indigenous Peoples and local communities, use and benefit from biodiversity. National Ecosystem Assessments (NEAs) are nationally led processes that bring together scientific, government, local and traditional knowledge. They assess biodiversity and ecosystem services, their status and trends, drivers of change, impacts on people and the effectiveness of responses. By addressing national policy questions, NEAs aim to integrate the value of nature into planning and decision-making. The regional CARIBIO project, "Promotion of regionally harmonised approaches to the protection and sustainable use of biodiversity in CARICOM member states", is financed by Germany"s Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by GIZ. Led by the Caribbean Community (CARICOM), it runs from July 2025 to June 2028. Its outputs include strengthening CARICOM"s coordination role, promoting NEAs in national development planning and supporting access and benefit-sharing mechanisms in selected member states. The project builds on the experience of Grenada which conducted the Caribbean"s first NEA in 2019-2023, and on lessons from other countries. The Grenada experience showed the need to adapt guidance to small-island contexts, where published data and national expertise may be limited. It also demonstrated how surveys, interviews, workshops and participatory mapping can complement scientific research and government data, strengthen local ownership and improve the relevance of findings. Lessons learned will be shared through CARICOM"s sub-regional Technical and Scientific Cooperation Centre, the PANORAMA knowledge platform and the Sub-Global Assessment Network to inform future assessments and regional cooperation.

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – PTB - Neubau Zeitzentrum (Scheibe-Bau) - Projektsteuerung + BIM-Management -TNW
description: Gegenstand des Auftrags ist die Erbringung von Projektsteuerungsleistungen sowie das BIM-Management (Building Information Modeling) für den Neubau "Zeitzentrum (Scheibe-Bau)" auf dem Gelände der Physikalisch-Technischen Bundesanstalt (PTB) in Braunschweig. Die Physikalisch Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB) ist eines der weltweit führenden Metrologie - Institute und dem Geschäftsbereich des Bundesministeriums für Wirtschaft und Klimaschutz unterstellt. Standorte befinden sich in Braunschweig und Berlin. In dem Neubau "Zeitzentrum" (Scheibe-Bau) sollen die Tätigkeiten ausgeführt werden, die der Erfüllung der gesetzlichen Aufgaben der PTB im Themenbereich Zeit und Frequenz laut EinhZeitG (deutsches Gesetz über die Einheiten im Messwesen und die Zeitbestimmung) dienen, zusammen mit Aufgaben aus Forschung und Entwicklung, die für die Weiterentwicklung des Arbeitsgebiets notwendig sind. Bei der Bauaufgabe handelt es sich um den Neubau des "Zeitzentrums" (Scheibe-Bau) auf dem Gelände der Physikalisch Technischen Bundesanstalt (PTB) - Bundesallee 100 in Braunschweig. Im westlichen Teil der Liegenschaft befindet sich das Baufeld für den Neubau des Zeitzentrums. Der Neubau wird an der Stelle des Giebe-Baus errichtet, der vor Baubeginn zurück gebaut werden muss. Dieser Abriss findet außerhalb der Maßnahme "Neubau Zeitzentrum" statt. Das Baufeld besteht aus Teilbereichen bewaldeter Fläche und befestigter Flächen. Es handelt sich hier um relativ ebenes Gelände. Das Baufeld befindet sich in einer kampfmittelbelasteten Fläche. Der Neubau setzt sich aus Büro- und Laborräume zusammen. An die Messräume bestehen Anforderungen an die Schwingungsentkopplung der Fundamentierung, die Gewährleistung der Energieausfallsicherheit und strengen Temperatur- und Feuchteanforderungen. Zur weiteren Konzeptionierung des Gebäudes ist der Bedarf zur Ein- und Ausbringung von größeren Gerätschaften in die Messräumen zu berücksichtigen, z.B. bei der Planung von Flurgrößen und Deckenlasten. Ebenfalls ist der Bau eines begehbaren Ver-sorgungsgeschosses (Zwischengeschoss) mit Montageschienen einzuplanen Für die Liegenschaft der PTB liegt kein verbindlicher Bebauungsplan vor. Die Anforderungen an den Leitfaden Nachhaltiges Bauen, Barrierefreiheit sowie Kunst am Bau sind zu berücksichtigen und einzuhalten. Das Projekt wird mit BIM umgesetzt. Der Raumbedarf setzt sich wie folgt zusammen (Stand IPU): Büro/ Besprechung/ Funktionsräume und Labor- und Messräume (NUF) ca. 3.454 m² Technikfläche (TF) ca. 2.420 m² entwurfsbedingt Verkehrsflächen (VF) ca. 1.727 m² entwurfsbedingt Nettofläche (NGF) ca. 7.600 m² Arbeitsplätzen 91

title: Sweden – Footwear – Arbetsskor
description: Välkommen att lämna anbud i upphandlingen av arbetsskor! Vi välkomnar er att lämna anbud i vår upphandling av arbetsskor och tillhörande produkter för flera dalakommuner och bolag. Målet är att erbjuda ett ändamålsenligt och varierat sortiment som möter medarbetarnas behov av funktionella, bekväma och säkra skor i det dagliga arbetet. Upphandlingen omfattar arbetsskor för personal inom flera olika verksamhetsområden, bland annat tekniska förvaltningar, parkverksamhet, lokalvård, kostverksamhet, vård och omsorg, barnomsorg, socialtjänst, gymnasieskola och arbetsmarknadsverksamhet. Behoven varierar mellan verksamheterna och omfattar såväl arbetsskor med särskilda funktioner som skyddsskor anpassade efter arbetsuppgifternas krav. Utöver skor omfattar upphandlingen även tillbehör och skovårdsprodukter, såsom sulor, skosnören, broddar och andra relevanta produkter som kan bidra till god passform, säkerhet och hållbarhet. Vi ser fram emot anbud från engagerade leverantörer som vill bidra med ett brett och kvalitativt sortiment, god service och lösningar som möter verksamheternas behov. Varmt välkomna att lämna anbud – vi ser fram emot ett gott samarbete!

Las obras ejecutadas se acreditarán mediante certificados de buena ejecución, que indicarán el importe, las fechas y el lugar de ejecución de las obras y se precisará si se realizaron según las reglas por las que se rige la profesión y se llevaron normalmente a buen término; en su caso, dichos certificados serán comunicados directamente al órgano de contratación por la autoridad competente. A estos efectos, las obras ejecutadas por una sociedad extranjera filial del contratista de obras tendrán la misma consideración que las directamente ejecutadas por el propio contratista, siempre que este último ostente directa o indirectamente el control de aquella en los términos establecidos en el artículo 42 del Código de Comercio. Cuando se trate de obras ejecutadas por una sociedad extranjera participada por el contratista sin que se cumpla dicha condición, solo se reconocerá como experiencia atribuible al contratista la obra ejecutada por la sociedad participada en la proporción de la participación de aquel en el capital social de esta. El cómputo se efectuará hasta la fecha de finalización del plazo para la presentación de proposiciones u ofertas.

Estos certificados indicarán el importe, las fechas y el lugar de ejecución de las obras y se precisará si se realizaron según las reglas por las que se rige la profesión y se llevaron normalmente a buen término. El requisito mínimo será que el importe anual acumulado en el año de mayor ejecución, sea igual o superior al 70 por ciento del valor estimado del contrato.
